{{Short description|Model of asset returns}}
{{Technical|date=December 2021}}
In financial [[econometrics]] (the application of [[Statistics|statistical methods]] to economic data), the '''Markov-switching multifractal (MSM)''' is a model of asset returns developed by [[Laurent-Emmanuel Calvet|Laurent E. Calvet]] and Adlai J. Fisher that incorporates [[stochastic volatility]] components of [[Homogeneity (statistics)|heterogeneous durations]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Calvet | first1 = L. | last2 = Fisher | first2 = A. | doi = 10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00069-0 | title = Forecasting multifractal volatility | journal = Journal of Econometrics | volume = 105 | pages = 27–58 | year = 2001 | s2cid = 119394176 | url = http://archive.nyu.edu/bitstream/2451/26894/2/wpa99017.pdf }}</ref><ref name=CF2004>{{Cite journal | last1 = Calvet | first1 = L. E. | doi = 10.1093/jjfinec/nbh003 | title = How to Forecast Long-Run Volatility: Regime Switching and the Estimation of Multifractal Processes | journal = Journal of Financial Econometrics | volume = 2 | pages = 49–83 | year = 2004 | citeseerx = 10.1.1.536.8334 }}</ref> MSM captures the [[Outliers in statistics|outliers]], log-memory-like [[Volatility (finance)|volatility]] persistence and power variation of [[financial return]]s. In currency and equity series, MSM compares favorably with standard [[Stochastic volatility|volatility models]] such as [[GARCH|GARCH(1,1)]] and FIGARCH both in- and out-of-sample. MSM is used by practitioners in the financial industry for different types of forecasts.

== MSM specification ==

The MSM model can be specified in both discrete time and continuous time.

=== Discrete time ===

Let <math>P_t</math> denote the price of a financial asset, and let <math>r_t = \ln (P_t / P_{t-1})</math> denote the return over two consecutive periods. In MSM, returns are specified as

:<math> r_t = \mu + \bar{\sigma}(M_{1,t}M_{2,t}...M_{\bar{k},t})^{1/2}\epsilon_t, </math>
 
where <math>\mu</math> and <math>\sigma</math>  are constants and {<math>\epsilon_t</math>} are independent standard Gaussians. Volatility is driven by the first-order latent Markov state vector:

:<math> M_t = (M_{1,t}M_{2,t}\dots M_{\bar{k},t}) \in R_+^\bar{k}. </math>

Given the volatility state <math>M_t</math>, the next-period multiplier <math>M_{k,t+1}</math> is drawn from a fixed distribution {{mvar|M}} with probability <math>\gamma_k</math>, and is otherwise left unchanged.

:{| 
|-
| <math>M_{k,t}</math> drawn from distribution {{mvar|M}} || with probability <math>\gamma_k</math>
|-
| <math>M_{k,t}=M_{k,t-1}</math> || with probability <math>1-\gamma_k</math>
|}
 
The transition probabilities are specified by

:<math> \gamma_k = 1 - (1 - \gamma_1)^{(b^{k-1})} </math>.

The sequence <math>\gamma_k</math> is approximately geometric <math>\gamma_k \approx \gamma_1b^{k-1}</math> at low frequency. The [[marginal distribution]] {{mvar|M}} has a unit mean, has a positive support, and is independent of {{mvar|k}}.

==== Binomial MSM ====
In empirical applications, the distribution {{mvar|M}} is often a discrete distribution that can take the values <math>m_0</math> or <math>2-m_0</math> with equal probability. The return process <math>r_t</math> is then specified by the parameters <math>\theta = (m_0,\mu,\bar{\sigma},b,\gamma_1)</math>. Note that the number of parameters is the same for all  <math>\bar{k}>1</math>.

=== Continuous time ===

MSM is similarly defined in continuous time. The price process follows the diffusion:

:<math> \frac{dP_t}{P_t} = \mu dt + \sigma(M_t)\,dW_t,</math>
 
where <math>\sigma(M_t) = \bar{\sigma}(M_{1,t}\dots M_{\bar{k},t})^{1/2}</math>, <math>W_t</math> is a standard Brownian motion, and <math>\mu</math> and <math>\bar{\sigma}</math> are constants. Each component follows the dynamics:

:{| 
|-
| <math>M_{k,t}</math> drawn from distribution {{mvar|M}} || with probability <math>\gamma_kdt</math>
|-
| <math>M_{k,t+dt}=M_{k,t}</math> || with probability <math>1-\gamma_kdt</math>
|}

The intensities vary geometrically with {{mvar|k}}:

:<math>\gamma_k = \gamma_1b^{k-1}.</math>

When the number of components <math>\bar{k}</math> goes to infinity, continuous-time MSM converges to a multifractal diffusion, whose sample paths take a continuum of local Hölder exponents on any finite time interval.

== Inference and closed-form likelihood ==

When <math>M</math> has a [[discrete probability distribution|discrete distribution]], the Markov state vector <math>M_t</math> takes finitely many values <math>m^1,...,m^d \in R_+^{\bar{k}}</math>. For instance, there are <math>d = 2^{\bar{k}}</math> possible states in binomial MSM. The Markov dynamics are characterized by the transition matrix <math> A = (a_{i,j})_{1\leq i,j\leq d} </math> with components <math>a_{i,j} = P\left(M_{t+1} = m^j| M_t = m^i\right)</math>.
Conditional on the volatility state, the return <math>r_t</math> has Gaussian density

:<math> f( r_t | M_t = m^i) = \frac{1} {\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2(m^i)}}\exp\left[-\frac{(r_t-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2(m^i)}\right] .</math>

=== Conditional distribution ===

=== Closed-form Likelihood ===
The log [[likelihood function]] has the following analytical expression:

:<math>\ln L(r_1,\dots,r_T;\theta) = \sum_{t=1}^{T}\ln[\omega(r_t).(\Pi_{t-1}A)].</math>
 
[[Maximum likelihood estimation|Maximum likelihood]] provides reasonably precise estimates in finite samples.<ref name=CF2004/>

=== Other estimation methods ===
When <math>M</math> has a [[continuous probability distribution|continuous distribution]], estimation can proceed by simulated method of moments,<ref>{{cite journal |title=Regime-switching and the estimation of multifractal processes |last1=Calvet |first1=Laurent |first2=Adlai |last2=Fisher |date=July 2003 |journal=NBER Working Paper No. 9839 |doi=10.3386/w9839 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Lux 2008 194–210">{{Cite journal | last1 = Lux | first1 = T. | title = The Markov-Switching Multifractal Model of Asset Returns | doi = 10.1198/073500107000000403 | journal = Journal of Business & Economic Statistics | volume = 26 | issue = 2 | pages = 194–210 | year = 2008 | s2cid = 55648360 }}</ref> or simulated likelihood via a particle filter.<ref name="Calvet 2006 179–215">{{Cite journal | last1 = Calvet | first1 = L. E. | last2 = Fisher | first2 = A. J. | last3 = Thompson | first3 = S. B. | title = Volatility comovement: A multifrequency approach | doi = 10.1016/j.jeconom.2005.01.008 | journal = Journal of Econometrics | volume = 131 | issue = 1–2 | pages = 179–215 | year = 2006 | citeseerx = 10.1.1.331.152 }}</ref>

== Forecasting ==

Given <math>r_1,\dots,r_t</math>, the conditional distribution of the latent state vector at date <math>t+n</math> is given by:

:<math>\hat{\Pi}_{t,n} = \Pi_tA^n.\,</math>
 
MSM often provides better volatility forecasts than some of the best traditional models both in and out of sample. Calvet and Fisher<ref name=CF2004/> report considerable gains in exchange rate volatility forecasts at horizons of 10 to 50 days as compared with GARCH(1,1), Markov-Switching GARCH,<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Gray | first1 = S. F. | doi = 10.1016/0304-405X(96)00875-6 | title = Modeling the conditional distribution of interest rates as a regime-switching process | journal = Journal of Financial Economics | volume = 42 | pages = 27–77 | year = 1996 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Klaassen | first1 = F. | title = Improving GARCH volatility forecasts with regime-switching GARCH | doi = 10.1007/s001810100100 | journal = Empirical Economics | volume = 27 | issue = 2 | pages = 363–394 | year = 2002 | s2cid = 29571612 | url = https://pure.uva.nl/ws/files/3524906/21100_v60.pdf }}</ref> and Fractionally Integrated GARCH.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Bollerslev | first1 = T. | last2 = Ole Mikkelsen | first2 = H. | doi = 10.1016/0304-4076(95)01736-4 | title = Modeling and pricing long memory in stock market volatility | journal = Journal of Econometrics | volume = 73 | pages = 151–184 | year = 1996 }}</ref> Lux<ref name="Lux 2008 194–210"/> obtains similar results using linear predictions.

== Applications ==

=== Multiple assets and value-at-risk ===
Extensions of MSM to multiple assets provide reliable estimates of the value-at-risk in a portfolio of securities.<ref name="Calvet 2006 179–215"/>

=== Asset pricing ===
In [[financial economics]], MSM has been used to analyze the pricing implications of multifrequency risk. The models have had some success in explaining the excess volatility of stock returns compared to fundamentals and the negative skewness of equity returns. They have also been used to generate multifractal jump-diffusions.<ref>{{cite book|last1= Calvet |first1=Laurent E.|last2=Fisher |first2=Adlai J.|title=Multifractal volatility theory, forecasting, and pricing|year=2008|publisher=Academic Press|location=Burlington, MA|isbn=9780080559964}}</ref>

== Related approaches ==

MSM is a stochastic volatility model<ref>{{cite book|last=Taylor|first=Stephen J|title=Modelling financial time series|year=2008|publisher=World Scientific|location=New Jersey|isbn=9789812770844|edition=2nd}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Wiggins | first1 = J. B. | title = Option values under stochastic volatility: Theory and empirical estimates | doi = 10.1016/0304-405X(87)90009-2 | journal = Journal of Financial Economics | volume = 19 | issue = 2 | pages = 351–372 | year = 1987 | url = http://dml.cz/bitstream/handle/10338.dmlcz/135564/Kybernetika_39-2003-6_1.pdf }}</ref> with arbitrarily many frequencies. MSM builds on the convenience of regime-switching models, which were advanced in economics and finance by [[James D. Hamilton]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Hamilton | first1 = J. D. | year =  1989| title = A New Approach to the Economic Analysis of Nonstationary Time Series and the Business Cycle | journal = Econometrica | volume = 57 | issue = 2 | pages = 357–384 | jstor = 1912559 | doi = 10.2307/1912559| citeseerx = 10.1.1.397.3582 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|chapter=Regime-Switching Models | last=Hamilton | first=James  |title=New Palgrave Dictionary of Economics |edition=2nd | year=2008 |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan Ltd. |isbn= 9780333786765 }}</ref> 
MSM is closely related to the [[Multifractal Model of Asset Returns]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=A multifractal model of asset returns | last3=Calvet | first3=Laurent | first2=Adlai |last2=Fisher |first1=Benoit |last1=Mandelbrot |journal=Cowles Foundation Discussion Paper No. 1164 |date=September 1997 |ssrn=78588 }}</ref> MSM improves on the MMAR's combinatorial construction by randomizing arrival times, guaranteeing a strictly stationary process. 
MSM provides a pure regime-switching formulation of multifractal measures, which were pioneered by [[Benoît Mandelbrot|Benoit Mandelbrot]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Mandelbrot | first1 = B. B. | title = Intermittent turbulence in self-similar cascades: Divergence of high moments and dimension of the carrier | doi = 10.1017/S0022112074000711 | journal = Journal of Fluid Mechanics | volume = 62 | issue = 2 | pages = 331–358 | year = 2006 | s2cid = 222375985 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Mandelbrot|first=Benoit B.|title=The fractal geometry of nature|year=1983|publisher=Freeman|location=New York|isbn=9780716711865|edition=Updated and augm.|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/fractalgeometryo00beno}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|first=Benoit B.|last=Mandelbrot|author2=J.M. Berger|title=Multifractals and 1/f noise : wild self-affinity in physics (1963 - 1976).|year=1999|publisher=Springer|location=New York, NY [u.a.]|isbn=9780387985398|edition=Repr.|display-authors=etal|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/multifractals1fn0000mand}}</ref>
